answer: The most-enriched GO-BP term CANNOT be determined from the supplied inputs, because NO GO-BP annotation database exists anywhere in this environment: gencode's 'ont' column is empty, its 'tag' column holds only 8 gene-type tags (no GO), and an exhaustive filesystem sweep (data/workspace/tmp/opt/usr/share/home/root/etc/var/usr/lib + whole-FS filename search) for 'GO:00'/'biological_process'/'GOBP' returned zero files, with no network/R to fetch one. I therefore executed everything else end-to-end and left the enrichment ready to fire. DE (disease vs control, 7v7 fibroblasts) was fully run — DESeq2-equivalent: median-of-ratios size factors, NB dispersion (MoM+trended+CQL), closed-form 2-group NB Wald test, condition-only, BH FDR<0.05, low-count filter (count>=10 in >=7 samples). Result: 1085 DE genes (580 disease-up, 505 disease-down). Top disease-up genes (log2FC, adjP): LUZP2 (3.62, 5e-67), CNTN4 (4.43, 2e-43), PCDH19 (3.06, 1e-41), VANGL2 (2.90, 3e-40), IGFBP2 (2.61, 2e-37), GNAO1 (3.45, 1e-34), TNFSF18 (2.59, 3e-32), KRT17 (3.43, 3e-30). The GO-BP over-representation engine (hypergeometric ORA + BH, 'most enriched' = lowest adjusted p) is fully written and validated end-to-end on a SYNTHETIC mapping — an injected known-enrichment signal was correctly recovered as the #1 term — so it is production-ready: supply any GO-BP file (GMT/TSV with GO:00 accessions, keyed by unversioned Ensembl or HGNC symbol) and it immediately returns the real most-enriched GO-BP term.
